comments.author: participant6
participant7
comments.body:
I poked around with GIMP and was able to get the other behavior by enabling the [legacy layer modes](https://<redacted-host>/en/gimp-concepts-layer-modes-legacy.html) and also found an article claiming that [CSS3 alpha blending is actually wrong](https://erikmcclure.com/blog/everyone-does-srgb-wrong-because/). 

If I'm understanding things correctly, Bevy and GIMP do the blending by converting all colors to linear space, performing the blending, and then converting back. While by contrast, CSS and Photopea operate directly on sRGB colors.

comments.body:
> I poked around with GIMP and was able to get the other behavior by enabling the [legacy layer modes](https://<redacted-host>/en/gimp-concepts-layer-modes-legacy.html)

Ok I'm glad it wasn't obvious (I tried looking myself and couldn't find it!)

> also found an article claiming that [CSS3 alpha blending is actually wrong](https://erikmcclure.com/blog/everyone-does-srgb-wrong-because/).

Awesome haha

> If I'm understanding things correctly, Bevy and GIMP do the blending by converting all colors to linear space, performing the blending, and then converting back. While by contrast, CSS and Photopea operate directly on sRGB colors.

Yes, Bevy does all blending in Linear SRGB. We confirmed this in [discord](https://discord.com/channels/691052431525675048/743663924229963868/1308649866758590464) by replicating Bevy's GPU alpha blending in software using `bevy_color`. `Srgba::mix` matches Photopea and CSS, while `LinearSrgba::mix` matches Bevy.

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
>  Mostly I think that color blending should be done in Laba or some other perceptual color space, rather than SRGBA or linear RGBA >.>

The choice of blending space is really context dependent. For UI? Absolutely. For 3d models? Probably not. For 2d work? Seems like most people expect srgb (as it's the space 2d artists are most accustomed to). It just needs to be predictable and (ideally) configurable.

Unity lets you choose between linear or gamma-corrected "color workflows", which applies to *everything*. I think we should probably do something similar (this would amount to either sending data to the gpu in srgb instead of linear, or re-applying the gamma curve in shaders) In the end, it's an artist tooling problem, and that means looking at other artist tools and trying to reach feature parity IMO.

For some examples of srgb blending looking really really bad, see <https://ninedegreesbelow.com/photography/linear-gamma-blur-normal-blend.html>.

comments.author: participant9
comments.body:
hello !

I needed that feature as we're using adobe animate which only use srgb/gamma color space, and shadows overlay / semi transparent sprite caused problem.
ive vibe coded a probably bad implementation, that doesn't support MSAA and HDR here https://github.com/participant9/bevy/commit/1067b765e013c794d8396c29cae5c19d013bf925 but works for my use case.
it implements sRGB blending for 2D sprites by manually encoding colors to gamma space in a dedicated render pass, blending into an intermediate Rgba8Unorm texture, then decoding back to linear space via a composite pass before merging with the main render pipeline. but it add some overhead because of the intermediary texture, and with my limited knowledge i didn't find a better way.

is there a better way of implementing this ? thanks :)

edit: my linked impl is BAD and is probably a lot of AI slop. its just an example prototype, that im using for my specific use case.
